You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The method findWrapPos in HelpFormatter is responsible for finding a position at which to wrap text to keep lines within a specified width. The bug report points out that within the last while loop in this method (lines 936-941), there is a condition `pos <= text.length()` which allows pos to be equal to text.length(). Then it calls `text.charAt(pos)` on line 937, which will throw a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException since valid char indices are 0..text.length()-1.

This matches the failing test case testRenderWrappedTextWordCut, which uses a small width of 7 and a single long word "Thisisatest." that likely triggers this condition.

Looking at the relevant code snippet:
- The code tries to find whitespace or newline before `startPos+width` by decrementing pos.
- If none found, it tries to move forward from `startPos+width` until a whitespace or newline is found.
- The problem occurs because the forward loop condition allows pos to go up to text.length() inclusive, which causes text.charAt(pos) to throw an exception.

The bug report specifically identifies the error line as line 908 with condition `pos <= width` in the first if, but the main crash comes from the final while loop condition on line 937 using `pos <= text.length()`.

The fix suggested is to change the `pos <= text.length()` condition to `pos < text.length()` to avoid out-of-bounds access.

In summary, the root cause is an off-by-one error in the while loop condition checking for wrap position beyond string length, leading to an attempt to access charAt(text.length()), which is invalid.

The failing test triggers this condition because the text is one long word without spaces and a narrow wrap width, making findWrapPos resort to this loop and break on out-of-range index access.

No other recent bug reports are relevant to this character index out-of-bounds issue.

# Summary
- findWrapPos method has a while loop with condition `pos <= text.length()`
- Inside the loop, text.charAt(pos) is called, causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when pos == text.length()
- The failing test creates a scenario where wrapping long continuous words triggers this loop
- The bug report confirms the off-by-one error and suggests changing <= to < in loop condition

This analysis explains the source of the bug precisely using the test and code snippet.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The method HelpFormatter.findWrapPos attempts to find the best wrap position given a text segment and maximum line width. The bug report highlights that in the last while loop (lines 936-941), the condition is `pos <= text.length()`, but inside the loop `text.charAt(pos)` is called, which will throw a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when pos equals text.length() because valid indices are from 0 to text.length() - 1. The failing test, testRenderWrappedTextWordCut, uses a narrow width and a continuous long word without whitespace, which triggers this forward search loop in findWrapPos. As pos reaches text.length(), the call to text.charAt(pos) throws the exception. The correct condition should be `pos < text.length()` to prevent accessing beyond string bounds. Thus, the root cause is an off-by-one error in the loop condition in findWrapPos, directly causing the observed failure. No other recent bug reports relate to this out-of-bound character access.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
